title: Control Plane Performance Evidence

hot_paths.risk: high route volume can contend on transaction metric aggregation
hot_paths.candidate: keep route-pattern cardinality bounded and watch allocation/lock cost

hot_paths.risk: poll, lease, and append metrics run on assignment/store hot paths
hot_paths.candidate: keep store metric aggregation bounded and compare operation-level cost before optimizing

hot_paths.risk: task screens with many historical threads can over-copy progress lines while computing active SSE filters
hot_paths.candidate: prefer active stream target projection over full visible thread copies for subscription paths

hot_paths.risk: fine-grained provider progress can create many render/normalize calls
hot_paths.candidate: batch provider progress before rendering and preserve structured fallback behavior

hot_paths.risk: polling and long-poll waiters can create goroutine pressure or stale busy state
hot_paths.candidate: keep long-poll waiters off the actor critical path and watch waiter/goroutine count

hot_paths.risk: workspace SSE subscribers can amplify each progress event into visibility checks and non-blocking channel sends
hot_paths.candidate: measure subscriber fanout in local pressure before expanding live event payloads

hot_paths.risk: tool approval long-poll waiters can add timer and waiter-map pressure when provider tools request human decisions
hot_paths.candidate: keep approval waits bounded and watch goroutine/timer deltas under stalled approvals

assertions: endpoint/API contracts must not change for performance evidence work
lightweight benchmark evidence must run without live credentials
local pressure evidence must emit measured allocation, latency, CPU, goroutine, and subscriber-fanout findings
live load evidence must stay redacted and use aiagentload rather than ad-hoc curl loops
pprof collection must use loopback-only RIIDO_AI_SERVER_PPROF_ADDR
performance candidates must name the hot path, risk, existing evidence, and next verifier candidate

loop.observation: Control-plane already has isolated load, metrics, and benchmark evidence, but high-traffic risk candidates and local CPU/resource deltas are not emitted from one executable performance loop.
loop.hypothesis: A performance evidence sidecar can bind endpoint, DB/store, SSE, scheduling, progress, local pressure, pprof, and load surfaces into one generated audit and lightweight benchmark workflow without changing external contracts.
loop.execute: Verify hot-path files and benchmark/test functions, publish lightweight benchmark output, publish local pressure throughput/latency/allocation/CPU/goroutine/subscriber-fanout evidence with measured findings, expose pprof and live-load commands, and generate candidate optimization rows.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on missing benchmark coverage, missing local pressure evidence, missing pprof loopback contract, missing aiagentload live command, stale generated docs, or non-strict workflow artifacts.
loop.retrospective: This keeps performance work in an open loop first: measure resource pressure and rank hot paths before promoting repeated bottlenecks into closed-loop gates.
